sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: UPR LOW AND ASSOCD TROUGH OVER THE INTERMOUNTAIN W WILL BEGIN TO EJECT ENE TOWARD THE NRN PLNS ON SATURDAY. BELT OF MODEST MID-LVL FLOW ATTENDANT TO THE TROUGH WILL ARC FROM THE FOUR-CORNERS REGION TO THE GRTLKS REGION...EMBEDDED WITH NUMEROUS SPEED MAXIMA. DOWNSTREAM...A LOW-AMPLITUDE DISTURBANCE OVER THE NERN GULF WILL ACCELERATE WNW TO THE LWR MS VLY AROUND WRN EDGES OF THE SERN STATES SUBTROPICAL RIDGE. IN THE LWR-LVLS...A LOW OVER NEB AT 12Z WILL TRACK NEWD INTO CNTRL MN BY 00Z SUNDAY AND INTO THE UPR GRTLKS REGION BY DAYBREAK SUNDAY. THE WARM SECTOR WILL EXPAND NWD FROM THE CORN BELT INTO THE GRTLKS REGION. MEANWHILE...A CDFNT DEVELOPING ACROSS THE WRN DKTS AND NEB PNHDL EARLY ON SATURDAY WILL BEGIN TO MOVE SEWD DURING THE AFTN...REACHING THE UPR MS VLY...CORN BELT AND CNTRL HIGH PLNS BY EARLY SUNDAY.

sections.title: DKTS EWD TO THE GRTLKS REGION
sections.text: THERE WILL BE SVRL TSTM CLUSTERS ONGOING ACROSS THE REGION EARLY SATURDAY. PRIMARY ELEVATED MOISTURE TRANSPORT/WARM ADVECTION REGIME SHOULD EXIST ACROSS THE UPR MS VLY/GRTLKS REGION AND ASSOCD STORMS WILL SPREAD DOWNSTREAM AND WEAKEN OVER THE CNTRL GRTLKS DURING MID-DAY. VERY WARM TROPOSPHERIC TEMPERATURES /10-12+ DEG C AT H7/ NOTED OVER THE PLAINS AT 00Z WILL CONTINUE TO BUILD NEWD INTO THE UPR MS VLY ON SATURDAY IN WAKE OF MORNING STORMS. BENEATH THIS CAP... BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE CHARACTERIZED BY 70S DEW POINTS WILL ADVECT NWD AS FAR AS CNTRL MN AND MUCH OF WI. THIS MOISTURE WILL ARC CYCLONICALLY W ABOUT THE SFC LOW INTO AT LEAST THE ERN DKTS AND PARTS OF NRN NEB...SETTING THE STAGE FOR A POTENTIALLY VERY UNSTABLE AIR MASS. MID-LVL SPEED MAX EVIDENT OVER NRN AZ/SRN UT IS EXPECTED TO REACH THE CNTRL/NRN HIGH PLNS SATURDAY MID-DAY. INCREASING ASCENT TIED TO THIS IMPULSE WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR POST-FRONTAL TSTMS DURING THE MORNING OVER THE FAR WRN DKTS. MID-LVL LAPSE RATES WILL REMAIN STEEP AND EFFECTIVE SHEAR MODEST...SO ISOLD STORMS MAY PRODUCE HAIL. AS THIS IMPULSE TURNS ENE AND CLOSER TO THE TRIPLE POINT...INHIBITION SHOULD WEAKEN FOR SFC-BASED STORM DEVELOPMENT...PROBABLY OV

sections.title: LWR MS VLY
sections.text: AFOREMENTIONED MID-LVL WAVE MOVING FROM THE GULF INTO THE REGION WILL BE ACCOMPANIED BY A BELT OF 30-35 KT UNIDIRECTIONAL ESE FLOW ALONG ITS NRN PERIPHERY. WDLY SCTD TSTMS...BOTH ASSOCD WITH THIS SYSTEM AND ALONG SEABREEZE CIRCULATIONS...WILL LIKELY GROW INTO FAST MOVING TSTM LINES/CLUSTERS AND COULD GIVE ISOLD DMGG WIND GUSTS. ..RACY/JEWELL.. 08/08/2009

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: GRT BASIN/NRN RCKYS UPR TROUGH WILL SHEAR ENE ACROSS THE NRN PLNS AND UPR MS VLY THIS PERIOD AS SERN U.S. RDG BUILDS N INTO THE OH VLY. IN RESPONSE...A BELT OF MODERATE SW TO WSWLY MID LVL FLOW... WITH NUMEROUS EMBEDDED SPEED MAXIMA...WILL PREVAIL FROM THE CNTRL/SRN RCKYS ACROSS THE NRN/CNTRL PLNS TO THE UPR MS VLY/GRT LKS. ON THE SRN FLANK OF THE SE U.S. RDG...A DISTURBANCE NOW NEAR NEW ORLEANS SHOULD CONTINUE WNW ACROSS LA TODAY AND REACH THE ARKLATEX EARLY SUN. AT THE SFC...NRN PART OF COMPLEX/ELONGATED NOW OVER NEB EXPECTED TO REDEVELOP NEWD INTO SW MN/NW IA LATER TODAY...BEFORE CONTINUING ENE INTO WI EARLY SUN. TRAILING SRN PART OF LOW SHOULD SETTLE SLOWLY S INTO NRN/WRN KS. AS NRN PART OF LOW APPROACHES MN...WARM SECTOR WILL EXPAND FARTHER NE FROM THE CORN BELT INTO THE SRN GRTLKS. W OF THE LOW...SEVERAL WEAK COLD FRONTAL SURGES WILL REINFORCE LOW LVL NLY FLOW ALREADY IN PLACE FROM THE DAKOTAS SW INTO THE CNTRL HI PLNS.

sections.title: DAKOTAS/UPR MS VLY TO GRTLKS
sections.text: SCTD ELEVATED TSTM CLUSTERS NOW OVER ERN SD...THE UPR MS VLY AND UPR GRT LKS SHOULD MOVE/DEVELOP GENERALLY ESE ACROSS THE LWR GRT LKS LATER TODAY IN ASSOCIATION WITH ZONE OF ELEVATED MOISTURE TRANSPORT/WAA. THE STORMS SHOULD WEAKEN AS THE STRONGEST ELEVATED INSTABILITY LIKELY WILL REMAIN FARTHER W ACROSS MN/WI. NOSE OF WARM MID TROPOSPHERIC TEMPERATURES /10-12 C AT 700 MB/ NOW OVER PLNS AND PARTS OF THE UPR MS VLY WILL CONTINUE TO SPREAD ENE ACROSS THE UPR MS VLY IN WAKE OF MORNING STORM CLUSTERS. RICH BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE WILL PERSIST BENEATH THE WARM LAYER...WITH LOW 70S F DEW POINTS AND PW AOA 2 INCHES OVER IA AND ADJACENT PARTS OF MN/WI AND IL. LOW LVL MOISTURE ALSO WILL LINGER N AND W OF NEB SFC LOW OVER THE ERN DAKOTAS AND NRN/CNTRL NEB. A SERIES OF WEAK DISTURBANCES WILL TRACK NEWD FROM THE CNTRL HI PLNS TO THE ERN DAKOTAS/UPR MS VLY TODAY AND TONIGHT. INCREASING ASCENT WITH THESE IMPULSES LIKELY WILL SUPPORT ADDITIONAL POST-FRONTAL STORMS TODAY OVER THE WRN DAKOTAS. COMBINATION OF STEEP MID LVL LAPSE RATES AND MODEST CLOUD LAYER SHEAR SUGGESTS THAT SOME OF THE STORMS MAY YIELD HAIL. MORE SUBSTANTIAL STORM DEVELOPMENT SHOULD OCCUR THIS AFTN OVER CNTRL/ERN SD...AND THIS EV

sections.title: LWR MS VLY
sections.text: UPR LVL WAVE MOVING WNW ACROSS THE CNTRL GULF CST WILL BE ACCOMPANIED BY A BELT OF 25-30 KT MID LVL SELY FLOW ON ITS NRN PERIPHERY. SCTD TSTMS...ASSOCIATED BOTH WITH THIS SYSTEM AND WITH SEA BREEZE CIRCULATIONS...MAY GROW INTO RELATIVELY FAST-MOVING CLUSTERS/BANDS THAT COULD YIELD ISOLD DMGG WIND GUSTS THIS AFTN/EARLY EVE. ..CORFIDI/HURLBUT.. 08/08/2009

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: UPPER TROUGH OVER THE INTERMOUNTAIN WEST WILL MOVE EWD INTO THE NRN/CENTRAL ROCKIES AND BECOME SHEARED AS IT ENCOUNTERS AN UPPER RIDGE BUILDING NWD INTO MID MS/OH VALLEYS. BETWEEN THESE TWO SYSTEMS...A BELT OF MODERATE SW TO WSW MID LEVEL FLOW WILL PREVAIL FROM THE CNTRL/SRN ROCKIES NEWD TO THE GREAT LAKES REGION. A WEAK UPPER LEVEL CIRCULATION...LOCATED NEAR NEW ORLEANS...SHOULD CONTINUE WNWWD THROUGH LA DURING THE PERIOD. AT THE SURFACE...A COLD FRONT...CURRENTLY LOCATED IN THE NRN/CENTRAL PLAINS...IS EXPECTED TO EXTEND FROM NERN MN SWWD INTO SERN CO BY SUNSET.

sections.title: CENTRAL PLAINS NEWD INTO THE GREAT LAKES
sections.text: MORNING ANALYSIS AND WV IMAGERY SHOWED A STRONG MID LEVEL IMPULSE MOVING NEWD ACROSS WRN SD...AND IS FORECAST TO SHIFT INTO MN THIS EVENING. ELEVATED STORMS HAVE DEVELOPED AHEAD OF THIS FEATURE OVER PORTIONS OF NRN NEB/SOUTH CENTRAL SD AND SHOULD EXPAND NEWD IN ASSOCIATION WITH THE UPPER FORCING. THESE STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO REMAIN MAINLY NORTH OF THE SURFACE FRONTS UNTIL EARLY AFTERNOON...DUE TO STRONG CAPPING IN WARM SECTOR...WITH HAIL THE MAIN THREAT. AS THESE STORMS EVENTUALLY SPREAD/DEVELOP NEWD INTO MN AND WI...SURFACE BASED STORMS ARE LIKELY TO DEVELOP IN THIS REGION...ESPECIALLY SOUTH OF THIS MORNINGS CONVECTION. THE WARMING OF THE VERY MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER AND STEEPENING MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES...ALONG WITH DEEP LAYER SHEAR AT 50 KT...WILL BE FAVORABLE FOR INTENSE SUPERCELLS WITH A POTENTIAL FOR VERY LARGE HAIL...WIND DAMAGE. THE EXTREMELY MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER...EXTREME INSTABILITY...MLCAPES IN EXCESS OF 4000 J/KG...INDICATES TORNADOES ARE ALSO POSSIBLE...ESPECIALLY NEAR A WARM FRONT EXPECTED TO EXTEND E-W ACROSS SRN MN INTO SRN WI THIS AFTERNOON. THIS IS WHERE THE HIGHEST SEVERE PROBABILITIES FOR HAIL...WIND AND TORNADOES ARE LOCATED. INTENSIFYING LOW LEVEL JET AND CONTINUE

sections.title: NERN CO/SERN WY
sections.text: WINDS BEHIND COLD FRONT WILL BECOME ELY AND ADVECT MOISTURE WWD THROUGH THE DAY INTO THE FOOTHILLS. WITH HEATING...STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP NEAR THE FOOTHILLS LATE IN THE DAY AND GRADUALLY SPREAD EWD INTO THE NERN CO PLAINS. THE ELY BOUNDARY LAYER WINDS AND SWLY WINDS ALOFT WILL PROVIDE SUFFICIENT SHEAR FOR SUPERCELLS. THE STRONG SHEAR AND MODERATE INSTABILITY WILL BE MOST FAVORABLE FOR LARGE HAIL.

sections.title: LOWER MS VLY
sections.text: MORNING ANALYSIS CHARTS SHOW A STRONGER BELT OF WINDS ASSOCIATED WITH UPPER WAVE IN SERN LA. THOUGH OVERALL SHEAR WILL NOT BE PARTICULARLY STRONG...GRADUAL STRENGTHENING WIND FIELDS COMBINED WITH SEA BREEZE INTERACTIONS AND A VERY MOIST ENVIRONMENT...PW AOA 2 INCHES...MAY YIELD A FEW WET MICROBURSTS THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING. ..IMY.. 08/08/2009

sections.title: UPGRADED TO MODERATE RISK ACROSS SRN MN...SE SD AND WRN WI
sections.text: THE MAIN CHANGE TO THE OUTLOOK IS TO ADD A MODERATE RISK ACROSS SRN MN...SE SD AND WRN WI. A VIGOROUS SUPERCELL IS ONGOING JUST AHEAD OF A RUC ANALYZED VORTICITY MAX IN SE SD. THE STORM IS MOVING INTO A TONGUE OF STRONG TO EXTREME INSTABILITY OVER SW MN WHERE MLCAPE CAPE VALUES ARE ESTIMATED BY THE RUC BETWEEN 3500 AND 4500 J/KG. THIS COMBINED WITH STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND 50 KT OF VERTICAL SHEAR ON THE WOOD LAKE MN PROFILER SHOULD SUPPORT SUSTAINED SUPERCELLS WITH WIDESPREAD LARGE HAIL. SUPERCELLS THAT MOVE ACROSS THE AXIS OF STRONGER INSTABILITY SHOULD BE EFFICIENT PRODUCERS OF VERY LARGE HAIL. THE TORNADO THREAT SHOULD INCREASE AS A CAPPING INVERSION ERODES AND A WELL-DEFINED LOW-LEVEL JET STRENGTHENS THROUGH EARLY THIS EVENING. THE GREATEST THREAT FOR SUPERCELLS WITH LARGE HAIL AND TORNADOES SHOULD EXIST FROM INTERSTATE-90 NORTH TO THE RED WOOD FALLS MN AREA AND EWD TO MINNEAPOLIS AND EAU CLAIRE WI WHERE A SFC LOW IS FORECAST TO TRACK. SHORT-TERM MODEL FORECASTS ARE ALL IN AGREEMENT...INCREASING CONVECTIVE COVERAGE IN THIS CORRIDOR THROUGH EARLY EVENING WITH AN MCS DEVELOPING AND PERSISTING THROUGH THE LATE EVENING. AS THE MCS MATURES...THE WIND DAMAGE THREAT MAY INCREAS
